# Kitty Inc

Canvas idle/clicker game (Vite + TypeScript, no framework).

## Rule one: 60fps under the stress test

Everything in the game (crits, events, flashes, spawns, menus, HUD, features, startup, the first tap) must hold 60fps on a phone **under the stress test**: a maxed-out game (6 companies × 30 buildings × 20 floors, maxed workers and managers) with the coin-burst storm running. That busy state is the baseline, never a fresh save. Anything that drops below it is unfinished, however good it looks.

- **Measure** with the dev server running: `node scripts/crit-perf.mjs --warm <kind | event | run:<scenario> ...>` (no names: what git changed). It runs the stress rig by default (`--rig=late=1`, storm on; `--rig=` adds options) at 4x CPU on a phone screen. Pass: fps 58+, frame p95 within one frame, no hitches; fix every HOT or high finding from `scripts/perf-audit.mjs`. Runs swing ±5–15fps: re-run before fixing and before calling it done. `--rank played` (or `floor`, `income`, `button`, `lock`, `rate`, `events`) ranks every crit by what its frames cost (redraw p95, and what it adds over the game idle), SLOW ones first; a SLOW crit gets cheaper or goes.
- **Make the work cheap** in our own code, for every browser. The one gate: while frames run slow (`CONFIG.crit.procSlowFrameMs`), a new special crit can't proc until the crits playing and their rewards have finished (`shared/critLoad`, checked in the rolls); no other gate, budget, skip or delay of crits to protect the frame rate, and never instead of making a crit cheap.
- **In a draw:** build sprites, paths, gradients, glyphs and lookups once at arm or first use; no per-item `.map`/`.filter`/`.slice`/spread/closures; no sort (presort, or sort one reused array in place); no `indexOf`/`includes`/`find` in loops; no `measureText` (cache by text); skip what's past its window (`drawWispBetween`) and return early once done; never `ctx.filter`, `shadowBlur` or pixel readback.

## Code

- One folder per module under `src/`, one `index.ts` (split past a few hundred lines inside it). Shared code in `src/shared/<name>/`; modules import each other only through `shared/`. General, reusable code; never duplicate logic.
- `src/crits/`: `critTypes` (tiers, procs, rolling), `critFlash` (flash, text; the shake is `shared/screenShake`), `floorCrits` (tier crits, floor/building rewards, floor crits as lazy `floorCrits/crits/<kind>` played by `floorCrits/critPlayer`), `incomeCrits` (lazy `incomeCrits/crits/<kind>`, the same `critPlayer` with the total as their one bar; rewards in its `index.ts`), `badgeCrits` (badges, foils, capsule), `animatedCrits` (events, stages), `critKit` (the played crits' registry and reward targets). Outside `src/crits` import only its `index.ts` and the pure-data `crits/config.ts` (spread into `CONFIG`); inside, import directly. `crits/critIcons.ts` registers its icons with loadAssets when the crits load.
- Startup: `src/boot.ts` (a few KB) starts the first screen's downloads (`preloadFirstScreen`), then imports `main.ts`. `boot`, `loadAssets` and `utils` stay free of game and crit imports; what the first frame doesn't draw loads after it (`afterStartup`, `prepareSoon`, `loadWhenIdle`). Anything heavy the first seconds of play would hitch on (warm-ups, the audio device, the first chunks) runs behind the splash with `shared/preheat` (`preheat(task)`, budget `PREHEAT_MS` in `main.ts`). Static DOM (canvas, action bar, dialog shells, splash) is markup in `index.html` (perf/index.html reuses it via vite.config.ts). The badge catalog is lazy: startup knows only `critData/kinds.ts` (generated by `scripts/crit-kinds.mjs`); a badge's `CRIT_PROC_INFO` is undefined until `loadBadgeCatalog`/`withBadgeCatalog`; `critProcIcon(kind)` works without it. No module-level tables over every crit kind. Measure startup on `npm run perf:build` + `npx vite preview --mode perf` (`game:*` marks).
- Crit amounts only in `CONFIG.crit` (`src/crits/config.ts`; badge values in `badgeCrits/balance/<category>.ts`); a played crit's odds in its `meta.ts`.
- Every orb, wisp or travelling light is `shared/wisp`: `drawWisp(ctx, at, ms, now, size, heat?)` (`at(ms)` its path), or `drawWispTrail` + `drawWispHead`. Never hand-drawn.
- Every tap or swipe target hit-tests through `shared/tapTarget` (`tapHits`, `tapHitsMoving`, `swipeHits`); never a hand-rolled distance check.

## Look and feel

- **Visual drama is the point.** Every crit and event builds up and pays off: something charges (trembling, glowing, light and glitter pulled in, the rumble and shakes rising), the motion speeds up beat by beat, and it all ends in a climax (the biggest blast, hardest shake and loudest bang, landing the reward). Big, bold movement across the screen; never low-key. A crit that only moves bits around quietly, tidies, lines up or drifts, with no build-up and no climax, is boring and gets cut, however clever its idea.
- **Cluster blasts are the reference** (`floorCrits/crits/volcanoCrit`, `meteorShowerCrit`): hits quick-fire about 45–50ms apart all over the targets, each a `drawDetonation` with its own small shake, rolling without a gap, capped by one huge blast with the hardest shake.
- **Fast and dramatic:** hard and quick, building to impacts (`shakeScreen`, blasts, slams, sound). Nothing slow, gentle or drawn out.
- **White and gold:** wisps, coins, beams, bolts, bursts, glitter. No new effect colours, no drawn props (the screen-game styles excepted).
- **Never spin the view** (shake, slide, zoom only); **never build on text** (a callout is garnish).
- **Text moves like our coins** (`shared/coinFlip`): one solid piece on one smooth arch, one solid flip or in-plane turn. Never warp it (grow, shrink, pump, stretch, squash, tilt, sway, bend), steer it through tight turns or stall it.

## New images to crits

Work in progress lives in the gitignored `tmp/`; only `--apply` writes `public/` and `src/`. Look at one sheet per step, never at each image; don't build tools to replace looking.

1. **Intake:** raws (jfif/jpg/jpeg/webp/png) in the root or `tmp/`; `node scripts/crit-intake.mjs` → `tmp/_sheets/intake.png`.
2. **Name:** fill `category` and `name` of every `tmp/_intake.json` entry in one edit (an existing `public/crits/<category>/`, or a new camelCase one added to its main category in `badgeCrits/critData/groups.ts`; the build fails until it is), then `node scripts/crit-intake.mjs --move`.
3. **Scan:** `node scripts/new-crits.mjs --scan` → `tmp/_new-crits.json` (re-runs keep edits). Fix "already used" by renaming the raw; report byte-identical `skip` duplicates and leave them.
4. **Preview:** `node scripts/new-crits.mjs` → `tmp/_sheets/processed.png`; re-check each name against its art (rename the raw, re-scan).
5. **Fix poor cuts:** `node scripts/new-crits.mjs --custom <kind> ...` → `tmp/<category>/process-<kind>.mjs`; tweak and re-preview until clean.
6. **Apply:** `node scripts/new-crits.mjs --apply` (icons, stickers, silhouettes, badge entries, balance lines; Real-ESRGAN upscale under ~640×640; raws and scripts to `tmp/crits/<category>/`). **Never delete a raw** unless the user says so.
7. **Verify:** `npm run build`, check a few in the game.

Cut-out fixes (`cutOutCritIcon`, `scripts/lib/crit-cutout.mjs`):

- Enclosed white gap: `backgroundSeeds: [[x, y]]`, only if truly background (white hair, clothes, teeth look the same).
- Art off the frame edge eaten: `protectedRects` over that edge **and** `dropWhiteHalo: false`.
- Near-white art erased: key only the backdrop (`backgroundColor: [252,252,252]`, `backgroundColorTolerance: 6`), feather light pixels near it.
- Tinted/dark backdrop: `backgroundColor` + tolerance, or `darkBackgroundThreshold`. Frame/letterbox: `sourceRect`. Specks: `keepLargestComponent` / `dropEdgeComponents`.

Shipped icons: `node scripts/upscale-crits.mjs [kind ...]` (backups in `tmp/_upscale/backup/`; prefer re-cutting from a raw in `tmp/crits/<category>/`); `npm run build` rebuilds changed stickers and silhouettes (`scripts/sticker-sources.json`); sheets via `scripts/crit-overview.mjs` / `scripts/crit-residue.mjs [category ...]`; pin `template`/`group`/`tier` (ids in `scripts/lib/crit-templates.mjs`) only when the auto plan fits poorly.

## What each part is for

Every crit group, spawn and animation has one job; build to it and never blur it.

- **Animated crits are the break.** The only thing allowed to stop the game: a mental break from tapping, as crazy as possible. They always start on the dark frozen overlay (the screen freezes and dims before anything of the event shows, the game stopped), then go all out. With the game stopped they get the frame budget to themselves, so spend it on heavier effects than anything that plays during gameplay (still 60fps under the stress test).
- **Every other crit plays during gameplay** (floor, income, button, lock and badge crits): instantly gratifying and never in the way. The reward lands at once on its own targets (the bars, the total, the buttons, the locked floor) while the player keeps tapping; nothing to wait for, read, follow or do. Its props start at or next to those targets and everything lands on them; never cover, dim or darken the rest of the screen, fill it with screen-wide props, swarms or flashes, pull the eye away, block a tap or change how anything behaves.
- **Random spawns are the opt-in detour** (`src/spawn`): the chance to step out of the regular flow for a bonus. The player chooses to take it (a tap, swipe or hold on the spawn) or ignores it; it never stops or blocks the game.
- **The upgrade button never stops upgrading.** A tap on it upgrades at once, every time it can be paid (or is free); a hold repeats at its normal pace. Button crits may change its look (gold, a wiggle, their label in place of the price) and add to what a tap gives (more levels, a payout, better crit odds), but never stop, delay or replace the upgrade, take over the press or hold, or show it pressable when the tap can't be paid. Never draw anything over or around it.

## Events

**Goal:** a slot machine; every crit and event is a lever pull, a thrill from first frame to payoff, only ever beneficial (no losses, waiting, downsides or player input). Crazier is better, but a laggy event is worse than a boring one. In `src/crits/animatedCrits/events/*Event`, all distinct.

**Every event:** never confusable (its own motion, layout and beats, not a swapped prop or colour; compare against existing events first); share code (streams, wisp, freeze, spotlights), never looks; about 1.5–2.5s (flight-stage events longer). Each batch has events of every animation style plus a few **experiments** off the styles (simulations, puzzles, algorithms, self-playing games; say which). **Test buttons:** every new animated crit gets a `meta.ts` in its folder (`export default { label, isNew: true } satisfies EventMeta`; its button `#test-<key>-event`, the key the folder name kebab-cased without `Event`), every new played crit `isNew: true` in its `meta.ts`; both show under **New Effects** by themselves. Once the user has tested it, drop its `isNew`. `critTestActions.ts` renders every tab from data (the events' cards via `loadEventCards`); never hand-write button markup or keep a list of crits.

**Rewards:** vary them: cash, free levels (`upgradeFloorFree`), floor crit tiers, worker perma tiers (`promoteWorkerPermaTier`), hires (`recruitWorker`), unlocks (`unlockFloorFree`), or a mix. The reward lands on screen on the hit that gives it (a bar jolting with `+N Lvl`, a worker lighting up, a floor unlocking); finish on what got rewarded (total-readout finales for cash only). On `wispCover`: targets from `animatedCrits/eventRewards` (`findRewardBars`, `findRewardWorkers`, `levelsFor`) into `startWispCover({ bars, workers })`, landed with `cover.levels`/`tierUp`/`promote`, finished with `cover.slam(bar)`; hires via `findRewardHires` + `giveHire` (`drawRewardHires` in `drawOver`); a free floor via `findRewardLocked`, then `context.unlockFloorFree` from `onEnd`. `rewardMultiplier: 0` pays no cash and skips the total finale; a cash event ending elsewhere sets `endOnTotal: false`. Gate on targets with `canArm`.

### Animation styles

Every crit and event uses one; any style can pay any reward. Each style's lib is its own module in `src/shared/animationStyles/<style>`; a new style gets its folder there, a line below, its per-style rule and its name in `BASE_STYLES` in `scripts/crit-dist.mjs` and `STYLES` in `scripts/select-animation-style.mjs`.

- **Money** (`animatedCrits/cashFlow` `pourLine`, `cover.flow`/`trace`): cash as liquid: rivers, jets, pools, geysers of hundreds to thousands of coins.
- **Wisp** (`animatedCrits/wispCover`): wisps flying, chasing, orbiting, colliding; coins only as bursts.
- **Mix** (`cashFlow` `riverHead` + `wispCover`): a wisp leading, feeding, drinking or firing a river of cash.
- **Beam** (`shared/animationStyles/beam`): aim, sweep, scan, cut, lock on (Scanner, Orbital Strike).
- **Lightning** (`shared/animationStyles/lightning`): forking bolts in a blink, arcing, chaining; each strike a flash, crack and jolt (Chain Lightning).
- **Explosion** (`shared/animationStyles/explosion`): lit bomb wisps on fuses, then big, chain and cluster blasts (Fuse, Supernova, Chain Reaction).
- **Gunfire** (`shared/animationStyles/bullets`): wisp bullets in spirals, rings, fans, bursts, volleys, crossfire (Bullet Hell, Gatling).
- **Bounce** (`shared/animationStyles/bounce`): wisps ricocheting off edges, bars and workers, hopping, drop-bouncing (Screensaver, Superball).
- **Drill** (`shared/animationStyles/drill`): a drill head grinding into an actor, sparks gushing, punching through (Breakthrough).
- **Spray** (`shared/animationStyles/spray`): a nozzle wisp hissing gold mist that coats its target until it flashes (Airbrush).
- **Race** (`shared/animationStyles/race` `planRace`): wisps racing round things on screen, a chaser on the leader's tail (Curves).
- **Clutter** (`shared/animationStyles/clutter`): a mess of bits put in order: swept, sucked, shoved or tidying itself into a pile (Clutter).
- **Galaxy** (`shared/animationStyles/galaxy`): hundreds of stars orbiting a core on a tilted disk (Accretion).
- **Drawing** (`shared/animationStyles/drawing`): a big picture out of hundreds of dots, blazing onto the reward (Bullet Mosaic).
- **Charge** (`shared/animationStyles/charge`): one element gathering power, trembling, glowing and pulling light in, the rumble building with it, until it bursts at the climax (like the black hole spawn).
- **Portal** (`shared/animationStyles/portal`): twin gold rings; things dive into one and burst out of the other with their speed kept, looping or hopping (Warp).
- **Slice** (`shared/animationStyles/slice`): swift slash streaks cutting things in two; the pieces slide apart along the cut, glitter spilling from it (Cut Open).
- **Pull** (`shared/animationStyles/pull`): one element sucking particles and other elements into itself, a trickle then a flood, swelling as it swallows, then bursting (the black hole spawn, Lodestones).
- **Summon** (`shared/animationStyles/summon`): a magic circle of light drawn in one stroke, its rings turning against each other faster and faster until a pillar of light erupts out of it (Conjure).
- **Snowball** (`shared/animationStyles/snowball`): a ball rolling over things, everything it touches sticking on and turning with it, growing bigger and faster (Sticky Ball).
- **Ripple** (`shared/animationStyles/ripple`): drops of light splashing down, rings rippling out flat over what they hit, a drizzle quickening to a downpour (Raindrops).
- **Crush** (`shared/animationStyles/crush`): one element pressing down on another in slams, harder and deeper each, until it's crushed flat.
- **Flight** (`animatedCrits/flightStage`): first-person flight out of the floors, through the sky, crash-landing back (Lightspeed, Starfighter).
- **FPS** (`shared/animationStyles/fps` on the flight stage): an old-shooter scene: in through the floors, a showdown, out a door or hole (Doom, High Noon).
- **Road race** (`shared/animationStyles/race` street in `shared/animationStyles/fps`, flight stage): behind a racing wisp through coins and the finish gate (Road Race).
- **Shmup** (`shared/animationStyles/shmup` + `shared/animationStyles/bullets`, flight stage): waves of wisp enemies and a boss, from above (Sky Raid).
- **Rail shooter** (`shared/animationStyles/railShooter` + `createRaceWisp` in `shared/animationStyles/fps`, flight stage): a wisp low over a checkerboard plain, wisps swirling in from the horizon (Harrier).

Screen-game worlds (FPS, Road race, Shmup, Rail shooter) use palette colours; the player is always a wisp (`createRaceWisp` first-person, `drawWisp` from above), shots and blasts stay wisps and bursts. Elsewhere a bomb is a wisp over `drawLitFuse`, a bullet a wisp, a gun a muzzle flash, a drill `drawDrill`, a spray `drawSpray`, a broom `drawBroom`, a hole `drawGravityHole`, a star `drawStars`, a picture `drawDots`, a portal `drawPortal`, a blade `drawSlash`, a magic circle `drawSummon`, a drop `drawDrop`; never drawn props.

### Per-style rules

A style is a behaviour, never one look: like gunfire (spirals, rings, fans, volleys, crossfire), every crit in a style finds its own props, layout, motion and beats. Before building one, look at the style's existing crits (`node scripts/crit-dist.mjs --style <style>`) and make it unlike all of them. The rules below set what a style must feel like, and their examples are a menu, never a template.

- **Explosion** (Chain Reaction): every event combines big blasts (large `drawDetonation`s, never pops), chain blasts (each setting off the next with its own shake) and cluster blasts (one bursting into several). A shake and a bang on the frame each lands; pile the biggest at each climax.
- **Drill** (Breakthrough): a bit grinding through metal, heavy and slow. It stalls on the bite for a few hundred ms with rumbling shakes, then bores in about 8 shoves over 1.5s+, each a jolt; the head judders (a few px `ctx.translate` jitter, hardest in the stall); `drawDrillSpray` gushes hundreds of sparks out both sides the whole time it bites, building past 1 as it bores and fading about 300ms after it's through. Never thin the spray.
- **Race** (Curves): `planRace(line, raceMs, corners)`, never constant speed: flat out on straights, braking hard over each straight's last third, about 0.3 speed in tight hairpins round real things on screen, accelerating out, finishing above top speed. A chaser about 120ms behind. Corners get only a screech and jolts; save the blasts for the finish (leader big, chaser huge).
- **Clutter** (Clutter): a mess of hundreds of bits (over the whole screen, along the bars, in a pattern; vary it) put in order, fast and satisfying. Vary who tidies and how: a broom, ploughing wisps, a gravity hole, an invisible force (`simulateSweep` / `simulateClean` at arm), or the bits tidying themselves (hopping into stacks, rows or a picture), never a swarm of small wisps. Brisk beats, each a swoosh or click and a jolt; the tidied pile lands on the reward.
- **Galaxy** (Accretion): hundreds of stars (`scatterDisk` / `scatterArms`) on a tilted disk, varied between events; everything keeps to `disk.at` (Kepler) and changes orbit with `disk.drift`, never jumps. Beats come from the orbits (clumping, swallowing, slingshots, collisions), quickening; the payoff flings wisps off along `disk.heading` onto the reward. The stars turn, the view never does.
- **Drawing** (Bullet Mosaic): a big, instantly readable picture from `SHAPES` (outline or fill, varied; add new ones as unit-box loops; never letters or numbers) out of hundreds of dots that each move to their spot (bullets, a pen wisp, flying wisps, sprayed or rained glitter), faster and faster, each burst a click and a jolt; once complete it blazes (`drawDots` `blaze`) with a shake and lands on the reward.
- **Charge** (black hole spawn): one element the eye stays on (a wisp, a core, a bar, a button) gathers power over about 0.8–1.5s from `planCharge`, building slow then fast: it trembles harder (`trembleAt`), its glow swells (`drawChargeGlow`), light races into it quicker (`drawChargeStreaks`), things around it are pulled in. The vibration follows the build-up: `tickCharge` every frame shakes and buzzes harder and closer together as the charge rises, never steady and never a flat rumble; the climax is the hardest shake with a bang (`tickCharge` returns true), released at once into the payoff (a burst, wisps or a blast onto the reward). Floor-crit style groups pass their `r.shake`.
- **Portal** (Warp): rings always come as a pair, edge-on (`drawPortal`), opening fast; whatever goes in comes out of the twin at once with the same speed (`planWarp` legs, never a pause inside), a pop, jolt and whoosh at every pass (`drawPortalPass`). The build comes from the passes quickening (a loop through the same pair falling faster each time, or hops ring to ring); the last exit lands on the reward. No tunnels, vortices or drawn frames.
- **Slice** (Cut Open): swipes of 60–80ms (`planSlash`, `drawSlash`) in quick fire, each a flash, a jolt and a whoosh; what's cut splits at once and its pieces slide apart along the cut (`sliceOffset`), glitter spilling out of it (`drawSliceSpill`). Cuts build from single to crossing; the last is the biggest (a cross or a long cut through everything) with the hardest shake. No drawn blades: the streak is the blade.
- **Pull** (black hole spawn): one element (a wisp, a hole, a bar, the readout, a button) sucks everything round it into itself, like the black hole spawn: glitter, coins, cash, numbers, wisps, even the fill out of the bars, torn loose and dragged in on spiralling, stretching paths, a trickle then a flood, quicker and quicker, whatever tries to break free yanked back. The element swells, trembles and glows as it swallows, the rumble rising with it (`tickCharge`), the field shown by the streams themselves (`drawFieldLines`, `drawGravityHole`). The climax swallows the last of it, collapses to a point and bursts (biggest blast, hardest shake), landing the reward. What gets sucked in and how it moves is the show: vary it every time (snapping specks into a crust on twin poles is Lodestones' and Pull Up's).
- **Summon** (Conjure): the circle lies flat on the ground under the reward (`planSummon`, `drawSummon`), drawn fast in one stroke by a pen of light, then its inner ring and marks; it turns slow then whipping round (`summonTurn`), a jolt at every turn (`revs`) closer and closer, glitter rising off it quicker; the eruption is a pillar of light (`drawSummonPillar`) with the biggest blast and shake, landing the reward at once. No runes, letters or drawn props: rings, ticks and a star of light only.
- **Snowball** (Sticky Ball): the ball rolls in passes (`planSnowball`, `rollAt`), each from rest and accelerating, each quicker than the last, a jolt at each end; everything within reach sticks on as it passes (a pop and, every few, a click), turning with the roll (`drawSnowball`), the ball growing (`snowballRadius`). It ends rolling onto the reward and bursting there, the crust flung off in a rattle of blasts.
- **Ripple** (Raindrops): drops (`drawDrop`) fall a short way onto their targets, each landing with a splash (`drawSplash`), a tick and a flat ring rippling out over what it hit (`drawRipple`), the reward landing on it; the drops quicken from a drizzle to a downpour (`rainTimes`), then one huge drop from higher lands the biggest blast and a double ring. Rings stay flat; never a screen-wide wave.
- **Crush**: one element (a giant wisp, the readout, a bar, a button, a slab of light) presses down on another (a wisp, a pile of coins or glitter, the locked floor, a bar's props) in slams from `planCrush`, quickening, each wound up (`crushAt` `lift`) and driven in faster and faster, deeper every time (`crush`), the target springing back a little as the crusher lifts. Every slam is a white-hot contact line with glitter squeezed out of both sides (`drawCrushContact`), a shake and buzz harder than the last (`tickCrush`); cracks of light spread through the target as it gives (`drawCrushStrain`), a crushed prop squashing flat and wide (`squashScale`; never text). Nothing in a crush stays stiff: the crusher stretches as it drives down and squashes and wobbles on every contact (`crusherScale`, text too when it's the crusher), a pressing slab bows round what it presses; only wisps and glitter get crushed (never coins or any raster: they pixelate). Every move accelerates: the crusher rams in and drives down faster and faster, lurches at every give and blasts on through after the crumble. The last wind-up is the highest, the slam the hardest with a bang: the target crushes flat and bursts, jets of glitter blasting out sideways (`drawCrushBurst`), the biggest blast landing the reward. Vary who crushes what and from where (down, sideways, two closing in like a vice). Or a press (`planPress`): the crusher pushes without letting up, trembling harder (`trembleAt`), the rumble rising (`tickPress`), the target warping hard as it strains (`pressWarp`: squashing at the contact, bulging, buckling sideways, its parts tilting and shuddering, the crusher sagging), glitter oozing out (`drawPressGrind`), giving in jolts closer and closer, until it crumbles (`crumbleFrom`, `crumbleAt`, `drawCrumbleDust`). With nothing on screen to crush with, the crusher is a slab of light (`drawSlab`).
- **Flight** (Lightspeed): always `startFlightStage` (it freezes, dives, flies the sky and speed lines, brings the floors back and crash-lands; never rebuild these). Leave by the default dive or a `FlightEntrance` drawing the frozen floors (the stage holds the dark overlay for `windUpMs` first), camera readable. Everything flown past lives in depth (`project(view, x, y, z)`, sized by 1/z), few and bold, each meeting a pop or jolt. Land on the reward: cash as things are picked up (`spotlightTotal`), the rest from `onEnd`. About 3–4s.
- **FPS** (Doom): scenes from `shared/animationStyles/fps` quads drawn far to near, never hand-projected; solid, detailed walls with depth and trim; in through the floors' screen (doors, a shutter, a portal) with a head bob; three or so bold enemies, each fight a beat (wind up, `drawFpsGun` fires, a flash, `drawDetonation`, bang and shake, the last biggest); out through a door (`ownLanding`) or a hole (`flightStage/hole`). About 4–5s.
- **Road race** (Road Race): the street from `shared/animationStyles/race` on `shared/animationStyles/fps`, bent with `roadBend`; the floors zoom away straight into a race already flat out (no grid); the camera rides behind the racing wisp, faster and faster, round a bend to the straight; coins vanish when taken (no pop left behind); out through the finish gate's window (`ownLanding`). About 5s.
- **Shmup** (Sky Raid): `shared/animationStyles/shmup` on the flight stage, the floors shrinking away below on the way in and the stage's own landing. Waves that build (small, bigger, a boss) firing fans, rings and spirals, dozens of bullets at the climax; the player's wisp weaves on its own, never hit, its twin guns on the next enemy to fall; every kill a sized blast, bang and shake (`createBeats`), the boss in a chain or cluster. About 5s.
- **Rail shooter** (Harrier): `shared/animationStyles/railShooter` (`drawCheckerPlain`, `drawRailPillar`) with `shared/animationStyles/race`'s racer wisp, the view riding behind and above it on the flight stage, its own landing into a screen of the floors at the horizon (`drawFpsOpening`). Waves of wisps swirl in from the horizon, quicker each wave, each shot by a wisp from the racer into a blast and coins; a big finish blown apart in a chain. About 4–5s.

### Drawing libs

Draw with these (each module's header documents its API); never rebuild them inside an event.

- **Stages:** `animatedCrits/wispCover` (`registerWispEvent`, `startWispCover`: `burst`, `blast`, `total()`, `trace(paths, travelMs)` for dancing coins; test button via `wireEventTestButtons` in `main.ts`); `animatedCrits/flightStage` (`startFlightStage(key, floor, context, { flyMs, draw, onEnd, enter?, ownLanding? }, { spotlightTotal? })` returns a `FlightBeat`; `project(view, x, y, z)`; timings in `CONFIG.flightStage`).
- **Motion:** `shared/curves` (`bezier`, `alongRoute`, `catmull`); `shared/easing` (`lerp([a, b], t)`, `clamp01`, `smoothstep` (doesn't clamp), `easeIn`/`easeOut`/`easeOutCubic`/`easeOutBack`); `shared/coinTargets` (`ringTargets`, `sprayTargets`); `shared/eventBeats` (`createBeats(items, dueAt, fire)`, `tick(ms, now)` each frame).
- **Glow and impacts:** `shared/glowShape` (`createGlowSprite` at arm, `drawGlowSprite`); `shared/glowSprite` (`drawGlow`, stops hoisted to a constant); `shared/twinkle` `stampGlimmer` (set `"lighter"` once per loop); `shared/eventFx` (`drawWhiteBurst`, `drawExplosion`); `shared/screenFreeze` `drawFreezeDimmed` (stable key); `shared/shatter` (`createPane`, `drawCracks`, `drawShards`, `releasePane`); `shared/screenCopy` (`copyScreen` once, `drawScreenPart`).
- **Animation styles:** `shared/animationStyles/beam` (`drawBeam(ctx, from, to, width, alpha)`, `drawAimLaser`, `drawBeamFlare`); `shared/animationStyles/lightning` (`createBolt` at arm, `drawBolt`, `drawStrike`); `shared/animationStyles/lightningArc` (`drawLightningArc`, a bowed crackling channel that can fire, inside a light batch); `shared/animationStyles/explosion` (`drawDetonation(ctx, at, msSince, size, now)`, `drawLitFuse`), bangs from `shared/explosionBang` (sound + buzz together, never the sound alone); `shared/animationStyles/bounce` (`ricochet`, `ricochetThrough`, `hops`, `dropBounce`, each with `at(ms)` and `bounces`; `drawBounceSplash`); `shared/animationStyles/drill` (`planDrill`, `drawDrill`, `planGrind` + `drawGrind`, `drawDrillSpray`); `shared/animationStyles/race` (`planRace` with `at`/`msAt`; `drawRoadStreet`, `roadBend`, `drawFinishGate`, `createRaceWisp`); `shared/animationStyles/clutter` (`scatter*`, `sweepLane`, `planSweep`, `simulateSweep`, `drawBroom`, `simulateClean` with plough/hole/force, `drawGravityHole`, `heapSpots`); `shared/animationStyles/galaxy` (`planDisk`, `scatterDisk`/`scatterArms`, `disk.at`/`drift`/`heading`, `drawStars`); `shared/animationStyles/drawing` (`SHAPES`, `shapeOutline`/`shapeFill`, `penOrder`, `drawDots`); `shared/animationStyles/charge` (`planCharge(startMs, chargeMs, style?)`, `chargeAt`, `tickCharge(charge, ms, shake?)`, `trembleAt`, `drawChargeGlow`, `drawChargeStreaks`); `shared/animationStyles/portal` (`drawPortal(ctx, at, size, open, now, turn?)`, `drawPortalPass`, `planWarp(legs)` with `at(ms, into)` and `passes`); `shared/animationStyles/slice` (`planSlash(from, to, startMs, swipeMs?)`, `drawSlash`, `drawSliceSpill`, `sliceOffset(slashes, centre, ms, gap, into)`); `shared/animationStyles/pull` (`planSnaps(count, box, poles, startMs, endMs, reach)`, `snapAt(snap, ms, pole, size, into)`, `flingAt`, `drawFieldLines(ctx, a, b, alpha, ms, size)`, `scatterFilings`, `drawFilings`); `shared/animationStyles/summon` (`planSummon(startMs, eruptMs, turns?)` with `revs`, `summonTurn`, `drawSummon(ctx, summon, ms, at, radius)`, `drawSummonPillar`); `shared/animationStyles/snowball` (`planSnowball(passes, specks, reach)`, `rollAt`, `stuckAt`, `snowballRadius`, `drawSnowball(ctx, ball, ms, at, radius, size, alpha?)`); ## Crit rules

- **Seven special groups** fill the special slot (`CONFIG.specialCrits`) after a gateway hit; never blur their focus:
  - **Floor crits** (`floorCrits/crits`), only on a multiplier crit: the number plays out onto the income bars in view, every hit upgrading floors (levels, payouts).
  - **Income crits** (`incomeCrits/crits`), only on a cash crit: the green `+$` amount (its cash plus `CONFIG.crit.incomeCritSeconds` of the company's income per tier multiple) slams in, then plays out onto the total income readout, every hit paying its share. Never the bars or floors; never a multiplier number.
  - **Button crits** (`buttonCrits/crits`), only on a multiplier crit: the number plays out onto the upgrade buttons in view, every reward on a button (sure crits, free taps, charges, presses).
  - **Lock crits** (`lockCrits/crits`), only on a multiplier crit and only while the locked floor is in view: the number plays out onto the locked floor, every reward on it (free floors, a cheaper unlock).
  - **Rate crits** (`rateCrits/crits`), only on a multiplier crit: the number plays out onto every open bar in view (maxed ones too), every reward on a bar's rate (faster for a while or for good, bigger payouts; a timed or used-up one is a bar effect, `defineBarEffect` in `rateCrits/rateBonus`), never its levels. Each reward lands with `flipIncomeRate` (the readout turning over onto its new value), the quicker beat and props on the bar (see **Income bar states**).
  - **Badge crits** (`badgeCrits`): give badges, shown by the flash.
  - **Animated crits** (`animatedCrits/events`): full events on the dark frozen backdrop, any reward.
  - Floor, income, button, lock and rate crits share `critPlayer`; each group has its own `CONFIG.specialCrits` slot and cooldown (floor and income crits one, `floorCrit`). **A new one is one folder, `src/crits/<group>Crits/crits/<kind>/`, and nothing else:** `meta.ts` (`export default { label, chance, style, values?, isNew: true } satisfies CritMeta`; `critKit` finds the folders with `import.meta.glob`, giving the rolls, the lazy loader and its test button, `data-<group>-crit`, perf `run:<group>-crit:<kind>`; no list of crits anywhere) and `index.ts` calling `registerFloorCrit(kind, { plan, draw, ...its reward })`. The reward is a hook on that def, never code in its group: a floor crit's `levels(count, step)` / `ownLevels` / `payouts(step)` (default: the crit's multiple on every other bar); a button, rate or lock crit's `reward(t)` (a lock crit's on the floor it opened; `beforeOpen(t)`, `false` to leave it locked; `twoFloors`), `t` a `critKit/target` `CritTarget`: the floor, the hit (`own`, `step`, `tier`, `count`, `index`, `price`) and the reward on screen (`levelUp`, `punch`, `flipRate`, `flipButton`, `pay`, `payPayouts`, `hire`). Something a tap lands later is a tap perk the crit defines (`defineTapPerk(word, land)` in `buttonCrits/buttonBonus`, shared ones in `buttonCrits/tapPerks`); a bar's timed or used-up speed or payout a bar effect (`defineBarEffect`, shared ones in `rateCrits/barEffects`).
  - Only animated crits stop the game; every other group plays during gameplay (see **What each part is for**).
- **Income bar states:** a bar either fills (its readout `$amount/countdown`) or, once its interval is under `CONFIG.incomePanel.minIncomeIntervalSeconds`, shows full and beats like a heart (`shared/pressureBar`, readout `$/s`; extra speed folds into the payout); a maxed floor's bar is solid gold. Under the stress test nearly every bar is full or gold. Any crit or event that targets bars (rate crits above all) must read on every state: land its reward on the readout (one coin-flip turn to the new value), the beat (quicker), props on the bar (pips, sparks) or payout bursts, never on a fill moving or refilling. Its cell or test shows a filling, a full and a gold bar together.
- **Two layers:** a tier (`crit`/`mega`/`ultra`) sets free upgrades and multiplier; a proc (special crit) rides on a landed tier, shown only by the flash. Canonical list: `CRIT_PROC_KINDS`/`CRIT_PROC_INFO` (`crits/critTypes`).
- **Rolling** only via `rollCrit`: tiers rarest first, one `SPECIAL_CRIT_GATEWAY_CHANCE` roll, every proc independently, capped to `MAX_SPECIAL_CRIT_PROCS` with `pickAtMost` (never bypass).
- **Rewards** in `applyFloorCrit` via `CRIT_REWARDS` (`floorCrits/floorCritRewards.ts`); map/building effects in `floorCrits/buildingCrits.ts` (don't claim a floor-only proc works on the map). Always positive and instant; no two crits share an effect or description.
- **Badge data** `{ label, color, image, description }` in `badgeCrits/critData/<category>.ts` (startup); reward in `badgeCrits/rewards/<category>.ts` (after startup; they don't roll until it loads), reusing `rewards/rewardHelpers.ts`. Icons register automatically: no per-crit draw calls, preloads, menu entries or test buttons.
- **Names:** the image decides the label: fun and unique about who or what it shows, their look, pose, action or props ("Copycats" for twin tabby cat girls, "Heifer Headlock" for one cow girl pinning another). No money word unless the art shows money or the pun comes from it ("Moolah Maker" for a cow girl); no bare category or theme words, words the art doesn't show, numbers or near-duplicates. Label, camelCase kind and icon basename match; `node scripts/rename-crit.mjs <kind> "<New Label>"` renames everywhere.
- **Effect groups:** `GROUPS` (`scripts/lib/crit-catalog.mjs`) sets target shares; new crits go to the groups furthest under (upgrades and payouts are full). When a group's templates run out, add a group: a `BadgeRewardActions` action (`rewards/rewardHelpers.ts`, bound in `floorCritRewards.ts`), templates in `scripts/lib/crit-templates.mjs`, a `GROUPS` entry.
- **Odds:** a badge roll picks one of the four `CRIT_GROUPS` (`critData/groups.ts`: girls, food, misc, wealth) evenly, then a crit by chance (`rollBadgeCrit`). Image categories hold about 20–50 crits. Group odds match shares, bigger rewards rarer; `scripts/lib/crit-odds.mjs` sets every chance (`--apply`; `node scripts/rebalance-crit-odds.mjs` after manual edits), within about `0.0016`–`0.013` (Heavenly, the rarest, `0.0001`).
- **Icon files:** `public/crits/<category>/<kind>.webp` (~640×640 area), `public/stickers/…webp`, `public/silhouettes/…png`.
- **Draw the styles:** every new batch of played or animated crits starts with `node scripts/select-animation-style.mjs [count] [--groups a,b]` (default 8 slots, every group once). It draws each slot's group and style at random (thin styles likelier, none twice), and a reward for animated slots. Build each slot in the style it drew: never re-roll, swap or pick styles by hand, unless the user names them. Vary the beats too: don't reuse one structure across a list (such as bar by bar, quicker each, its own bar last).
- **Balance the mix:** `node scripts/crit-dist.mjs` shows the thin spots: the animation styles and rewards each group has fewest of (`--style <style>` / `--reward <reward>` list what exists). Played crits' rewards go to their group's thinnest. Tag every new crit so the report counts it: an event's CONFIG comment starts `<style>, <reward>: src/...` (styles as in **Animation styles**, rewards cash, levels, crit tiers, perma tiers, hires, free floors); a floor, income, button, lock or rate crit carries its `style` in its `meta.ts`. A list's pitch says which gap each idea fills.

## Idea lists

New ideas go in `docs/ideas.md` as a `## List N` section.

- **Animated ideas** (floor crits, income crits, events, anything whose look is the point) are ALWAYS pitched with the playground in the same turn: one `IDEAS.push({ list: "nextK", name, about, ms, shakes, draw })` each in `tmp/_playground/ideas.ts`, drawn with the game's libs, the list heading linking `tmp/_playground/ideas.html?list=nextK`. Never text only. Their groups, styles and animated rewards come from `scripts/select-animation-style.mjs` (see **Draw the styles**).
- **Everything else** (features, systems, economy, collection) gets a playground cell too, showing the feature in play; build nothing in `src/` until the user picks one.
- **Badges are random, unrelated images, not sets.** Never pitch completing a set, category or group, set bonuses, or a second collection; badges are the game's one collection.

Rejected ideas leave `docs/ideas.md` (their playground cells stay unless asked). An idea the user calls good gets built.

## Artwork prompts

Subject at most 184 characters, so the whole prompt is at most 480; name the crit before describing its art in any list:

"Flat vector cartoon of [SUBJECT], bold thick black outlines, cel-shaded flat colors with simple glossy highlights, vibrant saturated palette, clean sticker/game-icon style, centered composition, slight 3D depth but no gradients or textures, isolated on a plain solid white background, no shadows, no text."
